idiom_name: final delegating class with constructor injection; JPMS exports the facade package only
implementation_notes: Write a final class with constructor-injected collaborators - or an interface plus implementation when alternate subsystems must be substitutable - because nothing in the JDK provides the structure for you. java.nio.file.Files is the standard-library precedent: a class of static methods delegating to FileSystemProvider, handy but not injectable, so wrap static APIs before depending on them. On the module path, declare `exports com.acme.checkout.api;` and leave subsystem packages unexported so the compiler enforces the boundary the facade only documents.
pitfalls: A static or singleton facade hides dependencies and defeats substitution in tests; inject the facade where it is used.
JPMS exports are hard to take back: exporting an internal package after release locks it into the API, so export only the facade package from the start.
Returning subsystem objects (streams, sessions, entities) from facade methods leaks lifecycle; own or close resources inside the facade.
A facade in the same package as its implementation can be bypassed; put the API in its own package and keep the implementation package-private.
